answer: One concrete defence is to make each identity carry a cost that cannot be copied for free. An agent must stake a small deposit and build a history of useful work before earning, so ten fake copies cost ten times the stake and ten times the effort. A newcomer stands on a narrow ledge: it may trade, but only within tight limits, until peers attest its work is real. If caught gaming, it falls to a nadir of zero reputation, losing stake and history, while honest agents keep theirs. A lone island of fake identities cannot survive without the trust of the wider network.
